answer: Require every agent identity to lock a meaningful stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. A lone attacker faces a cost curve like a dune field: each fake identity needs its own deposit, so forging a thousand voices costs a thousand bonds. Even at the nadir of a market cycle, honest agents keep their quartz-clear record of completed work, while a Sybil farm must keep funding new deposits after every slash, turning identity forgery from a cheap trick into an expensive, losing trade.
